correctness.rationale: For m≥4, a size-(3m−2) mutually visible set in K_{m,m,m} is exactly the complement of two vertices in different parts: any same-part hole pair strands a selected pair without a missing intermediate vertex. Thus the fixed top token-sliding layer is the triangle-adjacency graph on 3m² host cross-edges, each vertex degree 2m, with 3m³ edges and m³ triangles. On (R^A⊗R^B)⊕(R^A⊗R^C)⊕(R^B⊗R^C), decomposition of each part into constants and zero-sum vectors yields adjacency eigenvalues 2m once, +m with 3(m−1), −m with 3m−1 and 0 with 3(m−1)². The simple 2m eigenspace proves connectedness; L=2mI−A and Kirchhoff give exact tree count m^[3(m−1)](3m)^[3m−1](2m)^[3(m−1)²]/(3m²). Independent direct graphs for m=4,5 reproduce degree, edge/triangle counts and numerical spectra; for m=4, exact reduced Laplacian determinants mod two large primes agree. The proof, not finite tests, covers every m≥4.
residual_risks: m=3 is a different feasibility regime; theorem is explicitly restricted to m≥4.
The finite numerical eigenspectrum is supporting evidence; infinite multiplicities follow from an exact invariant decomposition.
